        COME NOW, N12/P1 Intervenors (Party No. 635) and file this Motion to Correct

Attachment A to SOAH Order No. 31 that was filed on June 8, 2026 (“SOAH Order No. 31”).

1.      On June 3, 2026, N12/P1 Intervenors filed their Designation of Parties for Cross

Examination and Exhibit List (Interchange No. 5680) complying with the requirements of SOAH

Order No. 6 setting forth the exhibits that N12/P1 Intervenors intend to rely on and present during

the hearing on the merits (the “N12/P1 Intervenor Exhibit List”). A copy of the N12/P1 Intervenor

Exhibit List is attached hereto as Exhibit “A” and incorporated herein.

                     DIRECT TESTIMONY OF JOHN A. “MATT” MATTHEWS, JR.
                               ON BEHALF OF KLM GRIFFIN RANCH, L.P.
              Please state your name, title, and business address (and mailing address if different
=




              than your physical address).
NY




              My name is John A. “Matt” Matthews, Jr. I am the Manager of Merrick Davis Ranch
WwW




              Management, LLC, the general partner of KLM        Griffin Ranch, L.P.    I am authorized to
FB




              appear on behalf of the partnership. My business address is 400 Pine Street, Suite 900,
Oo




              Abilene, Texas 79601.
              Describe what role the partnership has in this matter.
oN




              The partnership owns real property in Tom Green, Concho and Menard Counties, Texas
              affected by Link P1 of the joint Lower Colorado River Authority/ Oncor Electric Delivery
              Company LLC proposed transmission line project known as the Bell County East Switch
              to Big Hill Switch 765-Kv line. This testimony is offered on behalf of KLM Griffin Ranch,
              L.P.
              In your position, do you have knowledge          of the real property interests owned        by

              partnership that are affected, or potentially affected, by the proposed transmission
              line at issue in this proceeding?
              Yes, I do.
      >




              Describe the real property the partnership that will be affected by the proposed
              transmission line in this proceeding.
      PUC   Docket No. 59475                                                               Matthews — Direct
                                                                                     KLM Griffin Ranch, L.P.
                                                                 Bell County East Switch — Big Hill Substation
                 The tract(s) affected by Line P1 of the proposed transmission line are Tract Nos. 175, 176,
                179,   189,   190,   190.1, 202, 203   and 267     However,   the ranch as a whole     encompasses
DY




                approximately 20,000 contiguous acres (the “Property”).              Based on the available project
WwW




                maps, Link P1 of the proposed transmission line crosses the Property approximately 6.5
KR




                miles directly through the southern part of the Property.
Oa




                What is the Property referred to?
                The Property is known as the Kickapoo Springs Ranch.
      Pr Or
AN




                How does transmission line Link P1 affect the Property?
                Link P1 cuts through the southern third of the Property.         It enters the Property at an angle
Oo




                in the southeast corner and then turns west.
0




                Describe      the current    use of the Property       that will be affected by the proposed
                transmission line in this proceeding.
                The Property is an active working cattle ranch. The Property has several houses on it,
                including the main ranch house.
                Does anyone live on the Property?
      e




                Yes, I live full-time on the Property.
                Describe      any    improvements      on    the   Property   near    Link   P1   of the   proposed

                transmission line.
                The main ranch house was built in approximately 1955. There are three other residences
                or houses on the property, in addition to some hunters’ camps. Near the main house on the
                headwaters of Kickapoo Creek is a wellhouse that dates back to the late 1800s.             There are
                also barns, working pens and other ranching-related improvements, including cross fences
                throughout the Property. There are also over 30 stock tanks and water features that have
                been constructed on the Property.           Each of the cross fenced pastures has water piped to
                them from water wells and windmills located on the Property.
                How long has your family owned the Property?
      ©




                My father purchased what is now the Kickapoo Springs Ranch in June of 1960 from the
                Henderson family.
                Who were the Hendersons and what is their significance to the Property?




       PUC    Docket No. 59475                                                                      Matthews — Direct
                                                                                             KLM Griffin Ranch, L.P.
                                                                         Bell County East Switch — Big Hill Substation
              The Henderson family was one of the original families that settled in Tom Green and
=




             Concho      County, Texas.   The Henderson family established what is now the Kickapoo
NY




             Springs Ranch sometime around 1880.
WO




             Since 1880 the Property has only had two owners?
BB



     ©




             Yes.
oT




             Aside from being one of longest continuously operated ranches in the region, is there
OO




             any other historical significance to the Kickapoo Springs Ranch?
on




             Yes. The Battle of Kickapoo Spring was fought on the Property.
     OP




             What was the Battle of Kickapoo Spring?
             In May 1870, there was a battle between the “Buffalo Soldiers” stationed at Fort McKavett
             and the Comanche Indians. The “battle” consisted of several skirmishes that occurred over
             several days and was fought near the headwaters        of Kickapoo     Creek located on the

             Property.
             Who were the Buffalo Soldiers and why is this important?
     e




             Buffalo Soldiers were African American cavalry soldiers.      The first African American to

             be awarded the Medal of Honor was a Buffalo Soldier.       His name was Sargeant Emanuel
             Stance.     He earned his Medal of Honor during the Battle of Kickapoo Spring.
             Can you describe your cattle operations?
     e




             Yes. I run between 220 and 400 pairs on the ranch. A pair is cow and her calf. Currently,
             I have 228 pairs on the Property, which is a little on the low end.     We raise them before
             sending them to the stockyard.      At any given time, we also maintain between 15 and 25
             bulls.
             How long have you been involved in the cattle business?
     ©




             My whole life. My family has been working cattle in north central Texas since the 1880s.
     Ge




             The Kickapoo Springs Ranch is not just a weekend hobby ranch for you is it?
             No.      This is my home and my life.
     ror




             What kind of range improvements have you undertaken in your cattle operations?
             Over the last forty (40) years, I have removed all of the invasive cedar and mesquite trees
             from the Property. We have focused on improving the native grasses and returning the land
             to its natural state.


     PUC   Docket No. 59475                                                                Matthews — Direct
                                                                                    KLM Griffin Ranch, L.P.
                                                                Bell County East Switch — Big Hill Substation
      Q.     How      much would you estimate you have spent removing the cedar and mesquite
=




            trees?
WY




     A.     I have spent well over a million dollars removing the cedar and mesquite trees on the
            Property.
KF




     Q.     What happened when you cleared all the cedar and mesquite trees from the Property?
Oo




     A.     The native grasses improved because they were not having to compete with the invasive
            trees.     I have also seen the flow of Kickapoo Spring increase by about 750 gallons per
on




            minute because there is more groundwater available.
     Q.     Do you have a hunting operation on the Property?
     A.     No.      We do not allow commercial or paid hunting on the ranch. We have about 1400 acres
            of high fenced pasture with stocked white tail deer that we previously brought in to improve
            the genetics on the Property. Friends and family hunt on the Property, but it is not available
            for commercial lease.
     Q.     Do you have any exotics on the Property?
     A.     No, not on purpose.       There are some free-ranging exotics that wander into the Property
            from time to time, but we try to eliminate them so that they do not compete with the native
            wildlife.
     Q.     Ranching sounds like it is not just a business, but a way of life for you, is that correct?
     A.     Yes.      My family has been in the ranching business since the late 1800s.      This is the only

            way of life I know, and J wouldn’t want to do anything else. It is hard but satisfying work.
            I try to do things the right way and respect the land.    I take great pride in maintaining the

            integrity of the Property and trying to preserve its heritage as an active working ranch.
     Q.     What effect will the proposed transmission line have on your ranching operations?
     A.     Link P1 crosses over several water wells, windmills and water tanks on the Property. The
            water wells are a part of the integrated watering system we have on the Property. Water is
            piped from these wells and tanks to pastures without water features.        If we lose the use of
            any      of these   water wells, windmills,   or water tanks,   it will affect the entire water
            distribution system through the Property.       Several of the pastures will be without water.
            Link P1 also crosses numerous cross fences on the Property.
     Q.     Do you have a picture of an affected water well?


     PUC Docket No. 59475                                                                    Matthews — Direct
                                                                                      KLM   Griffin Ranch, L.P.
                                                                  Bell County East Switch — Big Hill Substation
           Yes. The picture of the windmill attached as Exhibit 1 would be affected by the proposed
          transmission line.    This particular windmill is 280 feet deep.      Water is pumped into the

          concrete tank behind the windmill and then distributed by pipeline to several pastures that
          do not have wells.
          Are your water wells shallow or deep?
©



          The water wells tend to be deeper than average.       The wells that would be affected by the

          proposed transmission line range between 100-280 feet deep.             While water is plentiful

          when you can find it, the cost of replacement of these water wells would be significant.
          Has the Property ever been involved in any research programs?
©




          Yes. We have participated in a range management study with Texas Tech. A professor from
          Texas Tech studied the effect of the brush clearing we did on the native plants and range
          conditions.
          Does the transmission line span any lakes or stock tanks on the Property?
e




          Yes, Link P1 of the transmission line would cross over, or be very near to, at least 10 stock
          tanks we have built on the Property.
          Earlier in your testimony you          discussed    the Battle of Kickapoo       Springs   having

          occurred      on the Property.     Do you    have    any   known    archeological    sites on the

          Property?
          Yes. We have found a large volume of Native American artifacts on the Property over the
          years. There are Native American campgrounds located throughout the Property. We have
          found middens, campgrounds and other areas throughout the Property.               Near Kickapoo

          Spring there are indentions in the rock where the Native Americans ground corn and other
          grains.
          Have any of these archeological finds been studied or documented?
> oO




          Yes.      The archeological sites have been researched and excavated by Hardin Simmons
          University and the Texas Archeological Society.
          When did this occur?
ror ©




          My father authorized the studies in the early and mid-1970s.
          Do you have copies of the studies and the results of the studies?
          I do.     I have attached as Exhibits 2-32 copies of the summaries of the archeological digs
          and studies that have been conducted on the Property.
 PUC    Docket No. 59475                                                                    Matthews — Direct
                                                                                     KLM Griffin Ranch, L.P.
                                                                 Bell County East Switch — Big Hill Substation
              Would the proposed transmission line affect any of these documented archeological
—_




              areas?
NY




              Yes, Link P1 of the proposed transmission line crosses over or is very near to the site
WwW




              documented in Exhibit 32.
FB




              You have mentioned          Kickapoo   Spring several times, can you please describe the
Oo




              spring?
              The spring comes out of the ground on the Property to form the headwaters of Kickapoo
wAN




              Creek. The spring is natural and flows under natural pressure and fed by the groundwater
              on the Property.    The spring produces on average about 1500 gallons of water per minute.
Oo




              Since my family has owned the Property since 1960, the spring has never run dry. Even in
Oo




              the worst of the droughts, the spring has never run dry. In fact, since we began clearing the
              cedars and mesquite trees from the Property, we have seen the volume of the spring double.
              Are there other accounts of the spring?
      e




              Yes.     In doing research on the Property, later, it appears the early Spanish explorers first
              documented the existence of the spring around 1682.        Early settlers discovered the spring

              in the 1870s.    The Henderson family set up their ranching headquarters around the spring
              in the 1880s. The Native Americans have known about the spring long before the Spanish
              and the settlers arrived.
              Can you describe the area around Kickapoo Spring?
      ©




              There are some limestone rocks that come out of the ground at the base of the confluence
              of two hills.      The water flows up from these limestone rocks.         Over the years some

              improvements have been added to deepen the pool, add a channel, a pumphouse, and even
              a paddlewheel to pump the water uphill for use on the ranch. The water flows at about 68
              degrees year-round and comes out of the ground crystal clear. Small fish live at the mouth
              of the spring and there are other animals, like frogs, toads, snakes and others, that live

              around the spring.      Once above ground, the spring forms the headwaters of Kickapoo
              Creek. In many ways, the spring creates a very small unique “micro climate” in the middle
              of the otherwise dry part of the West Texas related to Kickapoo Spring.
              Has anyone ever documented the hydrology of Kickapoo Spring?




      PUC   Docket No. 59475                                                                   Matthews — Direct
                                                                                        KLM   Griffin Ranch, L.P.
                                                                    Bell County East Switch — Big Hill Substation
               Yes.     In 1984, in connection with a water dispute, I engaged an engineering firm, Camp
=




              Dresser & McKee to conduct a hydrology report. A copy of the report is attached as Exhibit
NY




              83.
WwW




              The reports shows a gradual decline in the water volume in the spring?                What has
BR




              happened since the date of the report?
On




              Since the report, as I discussed above, we began clearing the Property of invasive cedar
              and mesquite trees which are known to consume a large amount of water.             As we began
on




              clearing the cedar and mesquite, the water flow in the spring increased.       Today, Kickapoo
              Spring flows naturally at about 1500 gallons per minute.      By removing the invasive trees,
              we have literally been able to “save” Kickapoo Spring from being choked dry.
              What concerns you about the construction of the transmission line and its effects on
              Kickapoo Spring?
              The proposed transmission line will be built on the part of the property that form the
              recharge zone for the spring.   The water drains from the south part of the Property where
              Link P1 of the transmission line would be located north toward Kickapoo Spring.               The
              proposed transmission line crosses many of the draws and water channels that form the
              spring.     Construction over this recharge area could have detrimental effects on Kickapoo
               Spring.
              Do you have any known caves or sinkholes on the Property?
      e




              There is at least one small cave or sinkhole located in a waterway not far from where the
              transmission line would be constructed. A photo of this cave is included as Exhibit 34.
              Is this the only cave or sinkhole on the property?
      e




               Yes, to the best of my knowledge.      There may be others, but I cannot document them.
              However, the Edwards Plateau is known for having sinkholes and caves throughout the
               area.
               Can you describe the wildlife on the Property?
      ©




               The wildlife is typical for this area of the state. We have a very good native white tail deer
              herd. We do not hunt the Property commercially so there is not much hunting pressure on
              the deer.    We’ve tried to improve the herd through management.          There are feral hogs,
              bobcats, coyotes, raccoons, porcupines, rabbits, skunks, opossums, snakes and just about


      PUC   Docket No. 59475                                                                  Matthews — Direct
                                                                                       KLM   Griffin Ranch, L.P.
                                                                   Bell County East Switch — Big Hill Substation
               all kinds of animals.    With the focus on removing the invasive trees and improving the
=




              grasses, the wildlife has thrived on the Property.
NY




              What about bird life on the Property?
WwW



      e


              Again, we have most types of birds that are native to the area. We see wild turkeys almost
BR




              daily throughout the Property.      With the focus on improving the grasses and our range
oO




              management,      coupled with predator control, the native quail population is making                 a
oO




              comeback.    Additionally, we see dove, hawks of all varieties, Mexican Caracols, buzzards,
on




              vultures, barn owls and great horned owls, song birds and all kinds of native birds.             We

              have an abundant population of hummingbirds on the Property as well.              Occasionally, we

              have even seen a golden eagle on the Property.       I attached a photo I took of a golden eagle
              resting in a tree on the Property as Exhibit 35.
              In these transmission line cases, lots of people talk about the presence of endangered
              species on their land.     Do you have any endangered species on the Property?
              Not that I know of. For most of my life as a rancher, I’ve never wanted to know if I had
              an endangered species on the Property.        The habitat is there, but I don’t know about any
              endangered species, other than a pair of nesting bald eagles on the Property.
              You have a nesting pair of bald eagles on the Property?
      e




              Yes, there is a nesting pair of bald eagles on the Property.      Their nest is located just north
              of where the proposed transmission line would be located. The eagles have been returning
              to the same nest each year for the past several years.       I have attached pictures of the bald
               eagles I took earlier this spring as Exhibits 36-38.
              The way you described the Property makes it sound “unique”.                 Is there anything else
              you’d like to add about the physical characteristics of the Property?
               I like to think it is a unique property.   It sits right at the edge of the transition of Edwards
               Plateau and the edge of the Hill Country. It has a blend of the characteristics of both areas.
